title: Closest to the Sun in January

lines.speaker: momo
lines.text: Seasons happen because Earth swings closer to the Sun, then farther away. Right?

lines.speaker: ravi
lines.text: Nope, not quite. This January third, Earth is the closest it gets to the Sun all year.

lines.speaker: ravi
lines.text: 147 million kilometres. And in July, 152 million.

lines.speaker: ravi
lines.text: It's the tilt. Earth's axis leans about 23.4 degrees, and that tilt causes the seasons.

lines.speaker: ravi
lines.text: Being closer gives about 7 percent more sunlight, but the tilt is what makes the seasons.

lines.speaker: ravi
lines.text: We're near the equator, so it's warm all year. In Colombo, January is about 2 degrees cooler than the warmest month.

lines.speaker: ravi
lines.text: Here, the year has four seasons, named for the monsoons.

lines.speaker: momo
lines.text: Closest to the Sun, in January. Who knew?
